questions.prompt: In Albion, what is the penalty each day for blocking a street, alley, sidewalk, or other public place without permission?
questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections:

No person shall encumber or obstruct any street, alley or watercourse, sidewalk or
               other public place by placing therein or thereon any building material or any article
               or thing whatever without first having obtained permission from the town council,
               the street committee or marshal of the town under a penalty of one dollar for each
               and every day such encumbrance continues. (Ord. 8 §1).

The street committee or town marshal is authorized to order any article or thing whatever,
               which may encumber or obstruct any street, alley or other public place, to be removed
               within one day after notice thereof to the owner thereof. It shall be the duty of
               the marshal of the town to remove or cause the same to be removed, to some suitable
               place, and the owner of any such article so removed, shall forfeit and pay to the
               town the sum of two dollars in addition to the expense of such removal which expense
               shall be recoverable in the action brought for such forfeiture and the defendant shall
               pay all cost of such action. Neither the committee of streets nor the town marshal
               shall grant permission to place or keep any building material in any of the watercourses,
               streets or alleys of the town for a longer period than three months. Such permission
               shall not authorize the obstruction of more than one-half of the carriageway and one-half
               of the sidewalk, except in cases of extreme necessity, and for short periods, and
               such permission shall be deemed void, whenever the period to whom the permission is
               granted shall extend the obstruction beyond the limits prescribed herein. (Ord. 8 §2).

questions.prompt: Is it legal to use a public street, sidewalk, or parking strip for your own private benefit in Black Diamond?
choices: Yes, if it does not block cars
No, it is unlawful without a right-of-way use permit
Only if you own the house next door
questions.answer: No, it is unlawful without a right-of-way use permit
questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections:

The purpose of this chapter is to establish minimum rules and regulations for controlling
               and enforcing right-of-way uses to assure that proposed uses are consistent with the
               public health, safety, and welfare of the community, and that harm or nuisance which
               may result from a proposed right-of-way use is prevented. It shall be unlawful for anyone to make private use of any public right-of-way without
               a right-of-way use permit issued by the city, or to use any public right-of-way without
               complying with all provisions of a permit issued by the city. ( Ord. No. 1182 , § 1(Exh. A), 10-6-2022)

The following words and phrases, wherever used in this chapter, have the meanings
               ascribed to them in this section except where otherwise defined or unless the context
               clearly indicates a different meaning. "Abutting property" means and includes property bordering upon and contiguous to a
               public right-of-way as defined herein. "Applicant" means any person, partnership, corporation, enterprise, entity, group,
               or agency applying for the issuance or renewal of a right-of-way use permit or any
               person, corporation, enterprise, entity, group, or agency that has been issued a right-of-way
               use permit. "Application" means the collection of papers or electronic data necessary to initiate
               a right-of-way use permit request, and includes an application in the form approved
               by the city and other submittals by an applicant consistent with the purposes of this
               chapter. "Private use" means use of the public right-of-way for the benefit of a person, partnership,
               corporation, enterprise, entity, group, or agency other than as a public thoroughfare
               for any type of vehicle, pedestrian, bicycle, or equestrian travel. "Right-of-way" or "ROW"…

questions.excerpt:
The purpose of this chapter is to promote pedestrian, bicycle, and public transportation
               travel to reduce negative environmental impacts, promote healthy living, advance the
               well-being of travelers, support the goal of compact development, and meet the needs
               of the diverse populations that comprise our community. It is intended to help achieve
               the goals and objectives of the City of Carnation (City) as a community in which all
               residents and visitors, regardless of their age, ability, or financial resources,
               can safely and efficiently use the public right-of-way to meet their transportation
               needs regardless of their preferred mode of travel. The City will plan for, design, construct, operate, and maintain an appropriate and
               integrated transportation system that plans for the needs of all users in new roadway
               construction, retrofit, or reconstruction projects. The system's design will be consistent
               with sound engineering principles and supportive of local neighborhoods, recognizing
               that transportation needs vary and must be balanced in a flexible, safe, and cost
               effective manner. (Ord. No. 877, § 1(Exh. A), 7-19-2016)

A "complete street" is a road that is designed to provide safe access to all users,
               including bicyclists, motorists, public transit vehicles and users, school buses,
               emergency responders, wheelchair users, and pedestrians of all ages and abilities.
               The complete streets concept focuses not just on individual roads but on changing
               the decision-making process so that all users are routinely considered during the
               planning, designing, building and operating of all roadways. Transportation facilities
               that support the concept of complete streets include, but are not limited to, pavement

Expand Chapters: 6.04 State Environmental Policy Act 6.08 Erosion and Sedimentation Control

Sections: Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 1851, §§ 1—23, adopted July 26, 2017, repealed the former Ch. 6.04, §§ 6.04.010—6.04.120,
               and enacted a new Ch. 6.04 as set out herein. The former Ch. 6.04 pertained to State
               Environmental Act Regulations and derived from Res. No. 754, §§ 1—12, adopted in 1984.

The district adopts this chapter under the State Environmental Policy Act ("SEPA"),
               RCW 43.21C.120 and WAC 197-11-904. This chapter contains the district's SEPA procedures
               and policies. The SEPA rules, Chapter 197-11 WAC, must be used in conjunction with

questions.prompt: Is it legal in College Place to turn into a parking lot or private driveway to skip an intersection or a traffic light?
choices: Yes, if you stay under 15 mph
No, unless proper authorities direct you to do so
Yes, as long as you do not block traffic
questions.answer: No, unless proper authorities direct you to do so
questions.excerpt:
_____

The "Washington Model Traffic Ordinance," Ch. 308-330 WAC is adopted by reference
               as the traffic ordinance of the city as if set forth in full. (Ord. 718 § 1, 1994)

It is unlawful for any person operating a motor vehicle upon the roadways of this
               city to turn such vehicle either to the right or to the left upon approaching or leaving
               an intersection and to proceed across any private property for the purpose of avoiding
               the intersection or any traffic-control device controlling the intersection, unless
               so directed by proper authorities. (Violation of this section is a traffic infraction.) (Ord. No. 19-017 , § 1, 7-9-2019)

_____

It is unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to operate a motor vehicle or a
               combination of motor vehicles having a maximum gross license weight in excess of 24,000
               pounds through the city on any of its streets. This restriction shall not apply to
               vehicles required to make deliveries within the city, the picking up of loads to be
               hauled outside the city limits, nor residents having such vehicles. (Ord. 561 § 1, 1985)

Any person, firm or corporation operating a motor vehicle or combination of motor
               vehicles through the city on any of its streets shall be able to produce a manifest
               or other document showing the gross weight of the vehicle and load being transported. (Ord. 561 § 2, 1985)

The chief of police and the director of public works for the city are authorized and
               directed to erect any signs necessary for advising the public of this chapter and
               the restriction. (Ord. 561 § 4, 1985)

Any person found violating this chapter or any amendment thereof shall be guilty of
               a misdemeanor, and upon conviction thereof shall be fined not more than $1,000.00.
               Each time a vehicle is used contrary to this chapter,…

               unoccupied building or parcel of land fronting as aforesaid, shall clean the sidewalk
               in front of or adjoining such building, or unoccupied lot or building, as the case
               may be, of snow or ice to the width of such pavement, by twelve noon of each day and
               cause the same to be kept clean from snow or ice; provided, that in case snow shall

questions.excerpt:
It is hereby declared to be the duty of the owners of property in the City of Duvall
               abutting on a public highway, street, lane, square, alley or place improved by the
               construction of a sidewalk or sidewalks along either or both sides thereof, to clear,
               repair and renew so that the sidewalk shall be a fit and safe means of public travel.

It is hereby declared to be the duty of the owner of property in the City of Duvall
               abutting on a public highway, street, lane, square, alley or place whether improved
               by a sidewalk or not, to keep all weeds, brush and vegetation of any kind cleared
               away and removed from such passage way of travel.

Should any abutting property owner fail, neglect or refuse to comply with 8.02.010 and/or 8.02.020 , the City Clerk shall serve upon the owner of said abutting property a notice to
               clear, repair, or renew any sidewalk or passage within ten days of the date of such
               notice.

The notice specified in 8.02.030 shall state a reasonable time in which such clearing, cleaning, repairing or renewal
               shall be executed by said owner. The notice shall further state that upon the failure,
               neglect or refusal of the abutting property owner to do such cleaning, repairing,
               and/or renewal within the time specified, such failure shall be reported to the City
               Council and that the Council shall proceed to take action as outlined in 8.02.050 . The notice shall state the date, place and time of the Council meeting where action
               will be taken and indicate that any and all protests against the proposed assessment
               will be heard at that time. The notice provided for herein shall be deemed sufficiently
               served if delivered in person to the owner of the property, or his authorized agent,
               or by leaving a copy of such notice at the…

As used in this Chapter, unless the context indicates otherwise: (1) Abandon means the knowing or reckless desertion of an animal by its owner or the causing

                  for the animal's adequate care. An animal left without adequate care for three or
                  more days shall be prima facie evidence that the animal has been abandoned. (2) Animal includes, but is not limited to, dogs and cats.                   of this Title. (4) At Heel means during such times as the dog is positioned and controlled in such a manner
                  so as to remain within a distance of two feet from its owner or other competent person
                  having charge of such dog. (5) At Large means off the premises of the owner or upon the public streets, alleys, public grounds,
                  school grounds or parks within the City. A dog shall not be deemed at large if: (a) It is attached to a leash or chain of sufficient strength to restrain the dog and
                  not more than eight feet in length, when said leash or chain is held by a person competent
                  to restrain and control the dog off the owner's premises; (b) It is properly restrained within a motor vehicle or housed in a veterinary hospital; (c) It is accompanied by and "at heel" beside the owner or a competent responsible person; (d) The dog or dogs are left unattended on the owner's premises, and it or they shall

               safety, and transportation requirements while prioritizing low impact development
               (LID) methods and practices. (Ord. No. 1541, § 1, 12-4-2017)

questions.prompt: In Mason County, leaving an animal without food, water, or care counts as abandoning it after how long?
questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections: Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 58-19, att. A, adopted June 18, 2019, added § 4.08.050 to the Code, and in
               so doing renumbered former §§ 4.08.050—4.08.170 as §§ 4.08.060—4.08.180, as set out
               herein. Prior ordinance history: Ord. 84-98.

This chapter may be cited as the Mason County animal code, to be codified as Chapter 4.08 . (Ord. 101-98 (part), 1998).

For the purpose of this chapter, the words and phrases shall be defined as follows: "Abandon" means the act of knowingly leaving an animal; (A) Without food, water, or care for twenty-four hours or more. (B) In a situation where conditions present an immediate, direct, and serious threat to
                  life, safety or health of the animal. "Abatement" means the termination of any violation by reasonable and lawful means
               determined by the animal control authority in order that an owner or a person presumed
               to be the owner shall comply with this ordinance. "Animal" means any mammal, bird, reptile or amphibian. "Animal control authority" means Mason County, Mason County's designee, acting alone
               or in concert with other local government units for enforcement of the animal control
               laws of Mason County or the state of Washington. "Animal control officer" means any individual employed, contracted with, or appointed
               by the animal control authority for the purpose of aiding in the enforcement of this
               chapter or another law or ordinance relating to the licenser of animals, or seizure
               or impoundment of animals, and includes any state or local law enforcement officer
               or other employee whose duties in whole or part include assignments that cover the
               seizure and impoundment of any animal. "Animal shelter" means a facility which is used to house or contain stray, homeless,
               impounded, abandoned or unwanted…

questions.excerpt:
A. Intent. The intent of this section is to clearly define animal classification categories
               and animal prohibitions within the city to ensure proper application and enforcement
               of this chapter and other city policies and regulations. B. Definitions. The following definitions and animal classifications shall apply throughout the city
               code, shall be in addition to any definitions adopted pursuant to other sections of
               this chapter, and shall supersede inconsistent definitions adopted by other sections
               of this chapter when this section 6.04.005 or the following definitions are referenced by other portions of the city code, specifically
               including Title 16 (Unified Development Code). 1. Domesticated animal or pet means a common domestic beast such as any dog, cat, rabbit, ferret, gerbil, hamster,
               miniature pig, parrot, chicken (excluding roosters), service animal, and other similar
               animals commonly treated and possessed as a domestic pet. Domesticated animal or pet
               excludes exotic animals and farm animals. 2. Exotic animal means any animal that does not meet the definition of "domesticated animal or pet"
               or "farm animal." 3. Farm animal(s) means any animal(s) that may be considered or defined as farm, barnyard, livestock
               or grazing animals, whether kept in open or fenced fields or grounds, or in structures,
               and regardless of use or purpose. Farm animal(s) includes without limitation cows,
               horses, mules, hogs, sheep, goats, roosters, and turkeys. C. Prohibitions. 1. No exotic animal nor any farm animal shall be raised, kept, maintained, harbored,
               used, or bred within the city. ( Ord. No. 996 , § 1, 7-12-2021)

questions.excerpt:
A. Purpose and intent. The purpose of this chapter is to ensure compliance with the city's adopted building,
               land development, land use, nuisance and related codes as specified in subsection
               B of this section, enabling the city to fulfill its duty to protect the health, safety
               and welfare of the public. These regulations establish procedures and mechanisms to
               resolve violations of the city's adopted building, land development, land use, nuisance,
               and related codes. This chapter establishes penalties for violations, provides an
               opportunity for a prompt hearing, decision, and appeal as to alleged code violations,
               provides for abatement when necessary, and provides a mechanism to recover the city's
               costs. This chapter shall be enforced for the benefit of the general public, not for
               the benefit of any particular person or class of persons. It is the intent of this chapter to place the obligation for code compliance on the
               person responsible for a violation, within the scope of this chapter, and not to impose
               any duty upon the city or any of its officers, officials or employees, which would
               subject them to damages in a civil action. B. Scope. This chapter may be applied for the purposes of enforcing chapter 8.24 MICC, Nuisance control code, MICC titles 15, Water, sewers and public utilities,
               17, Construction codes, 19, Unified Land Development Code, and other codes, ordinances,
               resolutions, permit conditions, or public rules that promote or protect the public
               health, safety or welfare and the environment. The provisions of this chapter are
               not exclusive and may be used, to the fullest extent permitted by law, in addition
               to other applicable provisions of the MICC or other applicable law or regulation. (Ord. 18C-06 § 2…

In construing this title, the definitions set forth in this chapter shall apply. (Ord. 302 § 1(part), 1976).

"Animal" includes animals of every description whether domestic or wild and whether
               spayed, neutered or otherwise, including fowl. (Ord. 302 § 1(A), 1976).

"At large" means other than under restraint by leash or chain or confined in a manner
               sufficient to prevent escape, outside the real property of the owner. (Ord. 302 § 1(B), 1976).

"Domestic animal" means those animals which are considered tame by reason of having
               lived with humans over many generations, and shall not include wild animals which
               have been tamed in a particular instance. (Ord. 302 § 1(C), 1976).

"Owner" means any person having any interest in the animal or any person having possession
               or control of an animal. (Ord. 302 § 1(D), 1976).

"Person" means any Individual or any combination of individuals, any corporation,
               partnership, association or firm. (Ord. 302 § 1(F), 1976).

"Stray animal" means any animal found at large without any apparent owner or home. (Ord. 302 § 1(E), 1976).

               town. (Ord. 253 §1, 1956).

The numbering system indicated on the map referred to in Section 12.04.010 is adopted as the block numbering system of the town; and there is established a
               system of numbering structures in the town: Commencing at the eastern and southern
               corners of each block, numbers are established for each twenty-five feet thereof,
               the numbers to commence with "1" on each northern and eastern boundary of each block,
               and every consecutive twenty-five feet shall have the next consecutive odd number,
               and the numbers to commence with "0" on each southern and western boundary of each
               block and every consecutive twenty-five feet shall have the next consecutive even
               number. The numbers shall be a portion of the block numbers designated on the official
               map, i.e., the first number in the twelve hundred block shall be "1200" on any particular

The Washington Model Traffic Ordinance, Chapter 308-330 WAC, is hereby adopted by
               reference as the traffic ordinance of the City of Port Angeles, Washington, as if
               set forth in full. (Ord. 2937, 1/1/1997; Ord. 2443 § 1, 5/1/1987; Ord. 2133 § 1, 4/1/1981)

The City Council is concerned about the safety of bicycle riders on public rights-of-way.
               Pursuant to RCW 35.75.010 the City may by ordinance regulate the riding of bicycles
               upon streets, alleys, highways, or other public grounds within the City limits. In
               order to protect the health, welfare, and safety of the residents of the City, it
               is necessary and appropriate to require bicycle riders to wear protective helmets
               and to establish programs for public education and low-income subsidies to promote
               the use of bicycle helmets. (Ord. #2764, 5/26/1993)

The following definitions are adopted for this chapter: A. "Bicycle" means every device propelled solely by human power upon which a person or persons
                  ride, which device has two tandem wheels, either of which is 16 inches or more in
                  diameter, or three wheels, any one of which is more than 20 inches in diameter. B. "Guardian" means a parent, legal guardian, or temporary guardian, who maintains responsibility,
                  whether voluntary or otherwise, for the safety and welfare of a person under the age
                  of 16 years. (Ord. #2764, 5/26/1993)

Beginning January 1, 1994, it is unlawful: A. For a person to operate or ride upon a bicycle on a public roadway, bicycle path,
                  or any right-of-way under the jurisdiction and control of the City unless wearing
                  a protective helmet of a type certified to meet the requirements of standard Z-90.4
                  of the American National Standards Institute or such subsequent nationally recognized
                 …

questions.excerpt:
(a) A developer extension agreement (DEA) is required in the following cases: (1) Subdividing property; (2) The development proposal is for a multi-family or commercial development; (3) A water and/or sewer main extension is required; and/or (4) Other activities as deemed appropriate for a DEA as determined by District staff. (b) Property owners and developers must apply for a DEA using the District's application
               form and pay the DEA application fee at the time the application is submitted to the
               District. The fee shall be in an amount as established by the Board of Commissioners
               from time to time. Any application for a DEA will not be received, accepted, or processed
               by the District until the application fee is paid in full to the District. (c) Property owners and developers entering into a DEA for construction extensions to
               the District's water and sewer systems shall use the most current standard developer
               extension agreement adopted by the Board and adhere to the terms and conditions set
               forth in the agreement. (d) Property owners and developers who enter into a DEA may be required to enter into
               special supplemental agreements contained in the DEA and may be subject to additional
               fees. (Res. No. 4303, 12-2-2013; Res. No. 4333, 4-7-2014; Res. No. 5031, exh. A(4.00.010),
               6-7-2021)

All short plats will meet the same conditions for water/sewer main installations,
               payment of general facilities fees and other fees as formal plats. This will be accomplished
               by requiring all applicants to enter into a standard developer extension agreement
               with the District. (Res. No. A-649, 1-13-1986)

The city council must start over
questions.excerpt:
Severability— The Land Use Code is declared to be severable. If any section, subsection, paragraph,
               clause or other portion of any part adopted by reference is for any reason held to
               be invalid or unconstitutional by any court of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity
               or unconstitutionality shall not affect the validity or constitutionality of the remaining
               portions of the Land Use Code. If any section, subsection, paragraph, clause or any
               portion is adjudged invalid or unconstitutional as applied to a particular property,
               use, building or other structure, the application of such portion of the Land Use
               Code to other property, uses or structures shall not be affected. (Ord. 110381, § 1(part), 1982.) Introduction: User Information The Land Use Code contains provisions typically associated with determining what use
            may be made of a person's property. It is organized in subtitles which describe the
            general provisions of Title 23 (Subtitle I), incorporate City approvals necessary for the division of land (Subtitle
            II), detail the establishment of zones and the use regulations and development standards
            applicable within zones (Subtitle III) and coordinate the administrative and enforcement
            procedures necessary to implement the land use regulations (Subtitle IV). While the provisions of Title 23 are integrated and extensive, they do not include all requirements conceivably related
            to development. For example, with the exception of the coordination of environmental
            review requirements in the Master Use Permit process, those regulations detailing
            construction specifications, i.e., building, grading, drainage, etc., are set forth
            in Title 22 , "Building and Construction Codes." Landmark districts and landmark preservation
            provisions are found in Title…

               within the rights-of-way in the city of Stevenson in the interest of public health,
               safety and welfare; 2. To provide for the enforcement, fees, charges, warranties, and procedures required

               adopted hereunder is intended to be or shall be construed to create or form the basis
               for liability on the part of the city of Stevenson, or its officers, employees or
               agents, for any injury or damage resulting from the failure of the permittee to comply
               with the provisions hereof, or by reason or in consequence of any act or omission

Chapters:

Sections:

The ordinance codified in this article shall be hereafter known as the transportation
               concurrency management ordinance and in the context herein may be referred to as this
               article. This article shall apply to all development which may affect any arterial,
               major collector, major rural collector, or public transportation routes within and
               adjacent to the city. (Ord. 463 Ch. 1 (part), 2001)

The purpose of this article is to prevent development from causing the level of service
               for any transportation facility having a functional classification, as described pursuant
               to Section 12.04.010 of this chapter, to decline below the standards established within the city comprehensive
               plan transportation element. (Ord. 463 Ch. 1 (part), 2001)

A. Administrative Official. The city clerk-treasurer, or a person designated by the clerk-treasurer,
               shall be the administrative official of this article and shall have the authority
               to administrate, interpret, and enforce all provisions herein. B. Fees. A review and processing fee of seventy-five dollars ($75.00) shall be required
               for a concurrency review of any development permit application which shall be paid
               in full to the city prior to the commencement of the review. Projects exempt from
               concurrency review shall not be subject to the review fee. (Ord. 463 Ch. 1 (part), 2001)

The Tieton city council shall have the sole authority to amend or repeal any or all
               parts of this article. (Ord. 463 Ch. 1 (part), 2001)

The following shall be exempt from the provisions of this article: A. Development permits issued prior to the effective date of the ordinance codified in
                  this article; provided the previously issued permit or permits have not expired. B. Construction of public transportation facilities. C.…

questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections:

A. This chapter shall be known as the Right-of-Way Use Code. B. It is the purpose of this code: 1. To provide for the issuance of right-of-way use permits in order to regulate activities
               within the rights-of-way in the city of White Salmon in the interest of public health,
               safety and welfare; 2. To provide for the enforcement, fees, charges, warranties, and procedures required
               to administer the permit process and ensure the long-term viability of public improvements; 3. To avoid creating or otherwise establishing or designating any particular class or
               group of persons who will or should be especially protected or benefitted by the terms
               of this code or any procedures adopted hereunder; C. It is the specific intent of this code and any procedures adopted hereunder to place
               the obligation of complying with the requirements of this code upon the permittee,
               and no provision is intended to impose any duty upon the city of White Salmon, or
               any of its officers, employees or agents. Nothing contained in this code or any procedures
               adopted hereunder is intended to be or shall be construed to create or form the basis
               for liability on the part of the city of White Salmon, or its officers, employees
               or agents, for any injury or damage resulting from the failure of the permittee to
               comply with the provisions hereof, or by reason or in consequence of any act or omission
               in connection with the implementation or enforcement of this code or any procedures
               adopted hereunder by the city of White Salmon, its officers, employees or agents. D. The provisions of this code shall be liberally construed for the accomplishment of
               these purposes and intents. (Ord. No. 2010-01-862, Art. II, 1-19-2011)

questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections:

A. Adoption by Reference. The Washington Model Traffic Ordinance, Ch. 308-330 WAC, is
               hereby adopted by reference as the traffic ordinance of the city as if set forth in
               full, except as provided in subsections (B), (C) and (D) of this section. B. Section Not Adopted. The following section of the MTO is not adopted by reference
               and is expressly deleted: 1. 46.90.275. C. Adoption of Additional Provisions. The following additional provisions are hereby
               adopted: 1. Sections 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11 and 12 of Ch. 275, Laws of 1994; 2. RCW 46.20.730 as amended by Section 23 of Ch. 275, Laws of 1994. D. RCW 46.55.113 Implemented. Pursuant to RCW 46.55.113, city law enforcement officers
               are authorized to impound vehicles whenever the driver of the vehicle is arrested
               for a violation of RCW 46.61.502, RCW 46.61.504, RCW 46.20.342, or RCW 46.20.420.
               The Woodland police chief or his designee is authorized to provide written direction
               to hold the vehicle for the time periods provided for and specified in RCW 46.55.113
               Section 2. (Ord. 893 § 1, 1998: Ord. 839 § 1 (part), 1997: Ord. 778 §§ 1—3, 1994)
